clue.text: Extremely small cape owned by Spanish artist

indicators.note: something owned by a person is held within their possession, so the cape sits inside the artist

parts.note: Joan Miró was a Spanish surrealist painter
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: A tiny headland turns out to belong to a Spanish painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefix-style adjective, now used alone, for things on a minute scale.

clue.text: Come along and cause something to break extremely painfully!

parts.note: to make it snap is to cause something to break

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cry of pain as someone snaps a bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely painfully' gives P and Y, the first and last letters of painfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are impatient instructions to hurry up.

clue.text: Looked right through one's skin

parts.note: to cut someone is to ignore them pointedly, looking right through them
one's read as 'one is' gives I and IS shortened to IS

explanation.surface: Someone stared right through another person's skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is I'S, the contraction of 'I is' with one as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutis is the anatomical term for the skin.

clue.text: Distinctive quality made to turn a woman's head

indicators.note: to turn something here is to read it the other way round

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness

explanation.surface: Something about a woman makes heads turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses TO into OT; 'made' is only a link. 'head' means a headland, not a person's head.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means the quality of being different or distinct from the rest.

clue.text: Elements taken separately from matchbox used by chemist

parts.note: a match in sport is a test, as in a cricket Test match
the box and the tube are both slang for television

explanation.surface: A chemist borrows the parts of a matchbox for an experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elements taken separately from matchbox' tells you to split matchbox into its two words and replace each with a synonym; a Test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass cylinder closed at one end is standard laboratory equipment for a chemist.

clue.text: Going off right away — doing this to find a station

definitions.text: doing this to find a station

indicators.note: right away tells us the letter for right is taken out

parts.note: milk that is going off is turning sour

explanation.surface: Someone sets off at once, looking for a radio station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'immediately' but takes R from TURNING.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjusting a radio's frequency to pick up a broadcaster is called tuning.

clue.text: High flier's reputation finishes fittingly on the up

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a name is a reputation, as in making a name for yourself
to cap something is to finish it off appropriately

explanation.surface: A successful person's reputation ends well as they rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the up' turns NAMECAPS into SPACEMAN; 'High flier' sounds like a high achiever, but he is literally high.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut flies higher than anyone, a playful sense of high flier.

clue.text: Had a crack checked out

definitions.meaning: to have a crack at something is to attempt it
a person ... and tested has been checked out

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both attempted and examined or tested.

clue.text: Personal growth after much bitter experience?

definitions.text: Personal growth after much bitter experience?

parts.words: Personal growth after much bitter experience
parts.note: bitter is a British beer, and the bodily growth from drinking lots of it is a paunch, not self-improvement

explanation.definitionFit: A paunch is blamed on heavy beer drinking, the growth from much bitter.

clue.text: Unofficial advisers giving order to be at check-in in time

indicators.note: putting jumbled things in order means rearranging them into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Someone is told to be at the airport check-in on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving order to' rearranges BE AT CHECK-IN IN into KITCHENCABINE, and T for time completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a leader's informal circle of advisers, as opposed to the official cabinet.

clue.text: Replaces word after revising one that has popular appeal

indicators.note: revising something reworks it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor swaps one word for another to win readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replaces word' reads as an editing instruction, but it is simply the anagram fodder; 'after revising' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that pleases the crowd is designed to appeal to many people.

clue.text: Cover one trained nurse can provide

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one

indicators.note: trained suggests shaped or reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A qualified nurse offers cover to a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' rearranges the nurse and can together into NSURANCE; 'provide' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance cover is financial protection against loss, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Stop British entering at great cost

indicators.note: one piece entering another goes inside it

parts.note: dear means expensive, bought at great cost

explanation.surface: Britain joins something only at a high price.
explanation.definitionFit: To debar someone is to bar or prevent them from doing something, a synonym of stop.

clue.text: Organized scheme involving limits of security check

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: to stem a flow is to check or halt it

explanation.surface: A security check is carried out according to an organised plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits of security' gives S and Y, which go inside STEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is a structured method or plan, the same idea as an organised scheme.

clue.text: In this respect a clergyman is a marvel

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A clergyman is praised as wonderful in one respect.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs inside 'reSPECT A CLErgyman'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is an impressive sight, something to marvel at.

clue.text: Ready to proceed? A must for solvent businesses

parts.note: ready is slang for cash, as in ready money
to flow is to move along steadily, to proceed

explanation.surface: A company being ready to go ahead is essential to staying solvent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is not an adjective here: 'the ready' is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A positive movement of money in and out is what keeps a firm able to pay its debts.

clue.text: Window-cleaners use buckets to wash

definitions.meaning: buckets are carried to contain liquid for washing
an argument that washes is convincing and stands up to scrutiny

explanation.definitionFit: Of an argument, to stand up to examination, as in 'that won't wash'.

clue.text: What's very often described in a plebeian manner?

definitions.meaning: something that happens usually or frequently
acting like ordinary or vulgar people

explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means both frequently and in a vulgar, low-class way.

clue.text: Hate, say, the Jewish religion

parts.note: to aver is to say or assert firmly
Sion, a variant of Zion, stands for the Jewish people and their faith

explanation.surface: Someone claims to hate a particular faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Aversion is strong dislike, close to hatred, so the nouns match.

clue.text: Cause problems resulting in stress

definitions.meaning: children or machines that misbehave are said to ...
to play something up is to emphasise or stress it

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to misbehave and to give extra emphasis to something.

clue.text: Born leader of Labour party rejecting second European 'war

indicators.note: rejecting a letter means throwing it out of the word

parts.note: Clement Attlee led the British Labour Party and was prime minister 1945-51
E is the abbreviation for European; 'second' says it is the later of the two Es that goes

explanation.surface: A Labour leader rejects a European war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' takes out the second E of ATTLEE to leave ATTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A battle is a fight between forces, standing for war in the clue.

clue.text: A favourite Queen Elizabeth put in prison cell

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: The Queen sends her favourite to a jail cell.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter is old criminal slang for a prison cell (also for a safe).

clue.text: A royal decoration mainly put over cooling dish

indicators.note: in a down clue, put over means turned upside down, reading the letters upwards
mainly means most of it, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a tiara is a jewelled headpiece worn by royalty

explanation.surface: A royal ornament is set on top of a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' cuts TIARA to TIAR, and 'put over' turns ATIAR upwards into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is an Indian yoghurt side dish served to cool a hot curry.

clue.text: Two spells at the same time?

parts.note: to spell is to signify or mean, as in 'this spells trouble'
a spell is a period of time, a while

explanation.surface: A question about casting two magic charms at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The two spells are different senses: the verb (signify) and the noun (a period of time).
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means during the same period, simultaneously.

clue.text: Friends spoiled billiards shot

parts.note: people who are in with each other are friendly
food that has spoiled has gone off

explanation.surface: Friends fall out over a game of billiards.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-off is a shot where the cue ball goes into a pocket after hitting another ball.

clue.text: Warning to be ready with cases outside the terminus

indicators.note: one piece outside another surrounds it

parts.note: actions are legal cases or lawsuits
a terminus is the end station of a railway line

explanation.surface: Travellers are warned to be ready with their luggage at the end of the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' suggests suitcases for a journey, but here it means lawsuits, split around the terminus by 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: The command calls a crew to their posts in readiness for battle.

clue.text: Hundreds of thousands of words, maybe, get misused

indicators.note: letters misused are put in the wrong order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone warns that a long text could be misused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misused' rearranges MAYBE and GET; 'maybe' looks like a qualifier on the definition but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of about a million bytes of storage holds text running to hundreds of thousands of words.

clue.text: Advert making a comeback too

indicators.note: the word reads the same when it comes back from the other end, so it is a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An old advertisement is being revived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advert' is the verb, as in 'advert to a point', not an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: To advert to something is to mention or allude to it, a synonym of the verb.
